name: CERT Bulgaria advisory context for DPRK fraudulent IT-worker risk

attribution.legal_posture: Threat-awareness guidance; legal and enforcement status, including a specific Bulgarian incident, requires a separate incident, regulatory, or court source.

caveats: Attribute the Bulgaria statement to CERT Bulgaria and disclose that the campaign detail is sourced to Insikt Group/Recorded Future.
This derivative article supplies an article-level context for PurpleBravo, TAG-120, TAG-121, malware and front-company discussion; record creation requires corroboration.
The page presents generalized risk claims; attribution of espionage, theft, extortion, backdoor installation, and operational disruption remains case-specific.
Nationality, appearance, accent, camera behavior, remote-work preference, and a single anomaly require corroboration before adverse attribution.

The article identifies Insikt Group/Recorded Future as its source. It is retained as an official Bulgarian national-CERT publication and geographic/defensive-context source; the underlying PurpleBravo, TAG-121, malware, victim, and front-company claims remain source-attributed rather than independent Bulgarian attribution.
The country-level location is retained solely because the official source expressly identifies Bulgaria in its generalized affected geography.

The Bulgarian national CERT includes Bulgaria in the affected geography and provides hiring and post-hire controls; Bulgarian victim, worker, facilitator, company, investigation, and enforcement identities remain unreported.
This record supplies advisory and geographic context; named incident, legal finding, sanctions designation, or actor attribution requires a separate source.
Use layered, lawful identity and access checks; public profiles exclude raw identity documents, addresses, payment data, and employee monitoring artifacts.

statements: CERT Bulgaria states that DPRK fraudulent IT-worker activity affects European states including Bulgaria.

The advisory describes false-identity remote hiring, referrals, third-party equipment delivery, substitute payees, avoidance of direct visual contact, legitimate remote-management tooling, and data-theft or extortion risk as generalized warning signs and risks.
It recommends layered identity verification, video interviews, least-privilege technical access, data minimization, anomaly monitoring, and coordinated HR and information-security awareness.
limitations: The campaign detail is materially derived from Insikt Group/Recorded Future and is not independent Bulgarian attribution of the underlying campaign, malware, victim, or front-company claims.
The advisory does not identify a Bulgarian victim, worker, facilitator, company, investigation, enforcement action, or confirmed incident.
No single behavior, tool, nationality, appearance, accent, camera issue, or remote-work preference establishes fraud or DPRK attribution.
Use lawful, proportionate, layered review with human adjudication; do not publish or retain raw identity, payment, or employee-monitoring data in public profiles.

sources.support: Bulgarian support: „Севернокорейски IT работници се внедряват в международни компании и си осигуряват дистанционни позиции под фалшиви самоличности. Сред засегнатите региони са редица европейски държави, включително България...“ The article also lists referral by a newly hired worker, delivery of equipment to a close friend, diversion of pay to accomplices, avoidance of face-to-face contact, camera excuses, use of JumpConnect/TinyPilot/RustDesk/TeamViewer/AnyViewer/AnyDesk, and identity, access, data-exposure and anomaly-monitoring controls. English translation: North Korean IT workers infiltrate international companies and obtain remote positions under false identities; affected regions include several European countries, including Bulgaria. The article additionally identifies referral, third-party equipment delivery, substitute payees, avoidance of in-person contact, camera excuses and legitimate remote-management tools, and recommends identity verification, video interviews, technical access controls, data minimization, anomaly monitoring, and joint HR/IT-security awareness. Translation note: Close researcher translation of reviewed Bulgarian official text; product names retained verbatim
